Figure 1:(Left) NLD-Uni introduces a new paradigm for building unified Diffusion LLMs through on-policy distillation from cross-paradigm teachers: VLMs for visual understanding and continuous diffusion models for visual generation.
(Right) NLD-Uni achieves highly competitive visual understanding and generation performance. Visual understanding performance is averaged across tasks in Table1. Text-to-image and image editing reports GenEval and ImgEdit Score. Multimodal reasoning is measured on MathVista. Axes are normalized by the best model’s performance on each task.

Figure 2:NLD-Uni supports diverse multimodal tasksby adopting an Elastic-MoT architecture with three elastic views of a single model. The VLM view uses the 8B understanding branch; the T2I view combines 4B understanding parameters with the 8B generation branch; and the interleaved view uses both full branches (16B). Each view loads only the parameters needed for its task. Yellow and green blocks denote understanding and generation layers, gray blocks indicate omitted layers, and blue arrows denote joint attention. Representative examples demonstrate visual reasoning, object grounding, text-to-image synthesis, and image editing guided by reasoning and localization.

Figure 6:On-Policy Distilling from Continuous Flow Models.Given a student output, we generate a teacher-refined output by adding noise to the student sample and re-denoise it with the teacher model. For reference, we also show an independent teacher generation. We observe that the teacher’s refinements are closely aligned to the student’s output while having better visual fidelity and source image preservation.
Figure 8:Qualitative Results on Text-to-Image Tasks. Results are sampled at1024×10241024\times 1024resolution.
Figure 9:Qualitative Results on Image Editing Tasks. For each input-output pair, we present the input image on the left and the output image on the right.

Figure 12:Visual Reconstruction Across Different Token Ages.To investigate whether the proposed age-based corruption process is semantically meaningful for visual generation tasks, we show reconstructed images at different token ages and compare them with the rectified flow process in the continuous latent space of Qwen-VAE. Results indicate that changes in the token age represent a smooth corruption process in the pixel space. In this visualization, all tokens are corrupted at the same rate, which corresponds toϵ=1\epsilon=1.

Figure 14:Additional Qualitative Illustrations of the Teacher Refinement Process.We show additional qualitative samples of teacher-refined student outputs. They generally align with the student roll-outs but have better visual fidelity and source image preservation. In some examples where the teacher over-edits, the refined student outputs are preferable to pure teacher generation.
